chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
That he was asked about tayammum, so he recited this verse:
"As for the male thief and the female thief, cut their hands."
"So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows."
And he said: "And wipe over your two palms from the place of the cutting."

key_terms.أَيْدِيَكُمْ: your hands, mentioned in the purification verse
key_terms.أَيْدِيَهُمَا: their hands, cited to clarify the Quranic legal usage of the term hand
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الْمَرَافِقِ: the elbows, the limit mentioned for washing the hands
key_terms.كَفَّيْكَ: your two palms, the area to be wiped in tayammum
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ الْقَطْعِ: the place of cutting, indicating the legal boundary intended
key_terms.نَسِيًّا: forgetful, negated from Allah in the cited verse
key_terms.وُجُوهَكُمْ: your faces, one of the parts addressed in purification

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith use Quran verses to explain where the hands are wiped in tayammum?
ai.summary: The hadith explains the ruling of tayammum by linking the wiping of the hands to the Quranic usage of "hand" in the verse of theft, indicating the extent meant in the command. It also cites the verse "And your Lord is never forgetful" to affirm that the divine wording is precise and deliberate in legal guidance.
